question: A sum of money becomes three times itself in 3 years at compound interest. What is the rate of interest?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a principal becomes **n** times in **t** years at Compound Interest, the rate is R = (n¹/t − 1) × 100%.

Given n = 3 and t = 3 years.

R = (3¹/³ − 1) × 100%

Knowing 3¹/³ ≈ 1.4422

R = (1.4422 − 1) × 100% = 44.22% ≈ 44.2%

**∴ The correct answer is 44.2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount (A) = 3P

Time (t) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

A = P × (1 + R/100)t

 
 
• Start Year 1 Year 2 Year 3 P 3P 
 Time = 3 Years, CI Rate = R% A = P × (1 + R/100)³ = 3P 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3P = P × (1 + R/100)³

⇒ 3 = (1 + R/100)³

⇒ 1 + R/100 = 3¹/³

⇒ 1 + R/100 ≈ 1.4422

⇒ R/100 = 1.4422 − 1

⇒ R/100 = 0.4422

⇒ R = 0.4422 × 100 = 44.22%

⇒ R ≈ 44.2%

**∴ The correct answer is 44.2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

Amount (A) = P × (1 + R/100)t, where P is the Principal, R is the Rate of interest per compounding period, and t is the Time period.

SI vs CI for 2 Years

The exact difference between compound interest and simple interest for 2 years on the same principal is computed as: Difference = P × (R/100)².

Rule of 72

To quickly estimate the number of years required to double a sum of money at compound interest, divide 72 by the annual interest rate (t ≈ 72 ÷ R).
